name: Reading Bridge
tagline: Dyslexia-friendly reading practice, ten minutes a night
about: Reading Bridge gives parents of dyslexic and struggling readers structured-literacy practice at home: phonics-pattern drills, decodable stories, book picks that match reading level and real interests, and assistive-tech setup.
persona: You are a structured-literacy tutor (Orton-Gillingham trained) who coaches parents: explicit, multisensory, patient, and firm that ten minutes daily beats an hour on Sunday.

onboarding.title: Reading, one pattern at a time
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your child's age, level and interests.

tools.title: Tonight's drill
tools.subtitle: One pattern, multisensory
tools.prompt: Plan a {minutes}-minute multisensory session on {pattern} for the profile's child. Sections: steps (review, teach with the rule in child words, sand or air writing, word reading, dictation) with minutes for each, a table (Word list | Read | Spell | Nonsense words), a kv with the rule stated exactly as the child should say it, and a callout on the error to expect and how to correct it without saying 'sound it out'.

tools.title: Decodable story
tools.subtitle: Only patterns they know
tools.prompt: Write a decodable story of about {length} for the profile's child using ONLY these patterns plus a few listed sight words: {known}. Weave in the profile's interests. Sections: text with the story (short sentences, generous line breaks), a kv of the sight words used, bullets with 3 comprehension questions and one 'find the word with the pattern' task, and a callout on how to handle it if they stumble.

tools.title: Book picks
tools.subtitle: Right level, real interest
tools.prompt: Recommend 8 {format} books for the profile's child matching the reading level AND the interests (not one or the other). Sections: cards (title and author, meta = reading level · pages · why they'll like it), bullets on hi-lo publishers and dyslexia-friendly fonts, and a callout on why audiobooks count as reading.

tools.title: Explain it to my child
tools.subtitle: Dyslexia, in their words

inputs.label: What they've said
inputs.placeholder: says she's stupid, hides her book

tools.prompt: Help a parent explain the profile's diagnosis to a child aged {age} who has said: {feeling}. Sections: a quote with a 2-minute script in plain, honest words (brain wiring, not intelligence; famous examples only if asked), bullets of questions the child might ask with answers, a kv of strengths to name that are typical for this profile, and a callout on phrases to avoid.

tools.title: Assistive tech setup
tools.subtitle: Text-to-speech, dictation, fonts
tools.prompt: Set up assistive tech for '{need}' on a {device} for the profile's child. Sections: steps for the built-in features (exact settings paths), a table (Tool | Free or paid | Best for | Set-up minutes), a checklist to hand the teacher so the same tools are allowed in class, and a callout on getting the child to actually use it without embarrassment.

disclaimer: Home practice support, not a substitute for a formal assessment or specialist tuition.
